title: The SvelteKit 3 Release Candidate is here
excerpt: We’ve cleaned out the junk drawer
content_html:
SvelteKit 3 is now in the Release Candidate phase. If all goes well — meaning that people like you try it out and find that it works as expected — we will follow it up with a stable release in the near future, with no further breaking changes.

But there are some breaking changes since SvelteKit 2. We’re taking advantage of this release to prune some of the weeds in the codebase and lay the groundwork for SvelteKit’s continued evolution, more on which below.

To migrate an existing app, you can use the next version of sv migrate:

npx sv@next migrate sveltekit-3 --tasks all --confirm

This will automatically migrate as much of your code as possible. For everything else, it will generate a TODO list for you (or your clanker of choice) to work through. Wherever possible, SvelteKit will print useful diagnostic warnings and errors if you try to run code that hasn’t yet been updated.

To create a new app, run sv create:

npx sv@next create my-new-app

What’s changed?

For the full list of changes, consult the migration guide over on next.svelte.dev which is where the SvelteKit 3 documentation will live until the stable release. Most changes are fairly minor, but a few are worth calling out:

Configuration now lives in vite.config.ts

Previously, you would configure SvelteKit via a svelte.config.js file. This turned out to be limiting: it’s useful for the Vite plugin to have access to your config immediately rather than having to go through an asynchronous resolution process (which can’t begin until after we’ve resolved the entire Vite config, because tools like Vitest may run with a current working directory that isn’t the project root), and after all why wouldn’t we put the config in one place rather than two?

The $lib alias is now #lib

In SvelteKit 2, you would put shared code in src/lib and import it via a $lib alias. This is nicer than importing from ../../../../somewhere, which is what inevitably happens in larger codebases.

But in modern projects, aliases are unnecessary, because we have something better: subpath imports. This Node feature is natively supported by tools like Vite and TypeScript, and it means we can delete the code that previously coordinated between them. There is one small gotcha: Node and TypeScript require that your subpath imports be unambiguous — instead of importing from #lib/foo, you will need to import from #lib/foo.ts or #lib/foo/index.ts.

TypeScript configuration got simpler

In SvelteKit 2, your tsconfig.json needed to extend the somewhat scruffy-looking ./.svelte-kit/tsconfig.json. In SvelteKit 3, you extend $app/tsconfig instead. This generated config file is written to node_modules/$app and contains configuration that is specific to your app. While it’s simpler than the SvelteKit 2 version (we no longer need to add the $lib alias to "paths", for example) it also includes more recommended compiler options, which means you can likely delete your own compilerOptions unless you have esoteric requirements.

You should explicitly specify your include and exclude arrays, and the latter should include your service worker. Speaking of which:

Service workers got a facelift

Using service workers is nicer in SvelteKit 3. Instead of the weird $service-worker module, which exposed the necessary tools to perform offline caching (for example), you can now just import those things from $app/env, $app/paths and the new $app/manifest module like in every other part of your app. You can also import self from $app/service-worker to get accurate typings for fetch events and so on, provided you create a tsconfig.json alongside your service worker that extends $app/tsconfig/service-worker.

In future, we may expose helper functions for different caching strategies, so that it’s easier to build things like offline-friendly PWAs without running into barbed wire.

Environment variables are more powerful

SvelteKit already had arguably the most sophisticated and flexible environment variable handling of any framework. SvelteKit 3 takes it a step further with the explicit environment variables feature, which are no longer behind an experimental flag. The gist is that you define which environment variables your app depends on, in src/env.ts, and specify if they should be publicly available (in which case you can import them into code that will run in the client) and whether they should be resolved at build time (in which case they can be used for optimizations like dead code elimination) or when the app boots up. You can also use Standard Schema libraries to validate your environment variables.

In exchange, you get effortless type-safe, secure, validated environment variables that can be auto-imported when you need them.

Error handling is way better

SvelteKit 2 was constrained by its support for Svelte 4, which didn’t have a concept of error boundaries. This meant that we could only display your +error.svelte components when errors occurred during load, not render. SvelteKit 3 requires Svelte 5, which means error handling can be made much more comprehensive and consistent.

Another change is that all errors are piped through your handleError logic, including the ones you deliberately created with error(...) which were previously ignored on the assumption that you’d already done something with them. This gives you more flexibility with less hoop-jumping.

Oh, and we apply sourcemaps to stack traces now. No biggie. (It’ll take a minute before every adapter can display properly sourcemapped stack traces in production, but this is the necessary first step.)

Shallow routing now happens with goto

Instead of using pushState and replaceState to use shallow routing, you now use goto with the shallow: true option. Shallow navigations now trigger beforeNavigate etc, and you can persist page state across a reload with persistState: true.

Vite 8: Rolldown, and the Environment API

SvelteKit 2 supported Vite 8, but SvelteKit 3 requires it. This means you get faster builds thanks to Rolldown.

We’ve also adopted the Vite Environment API, which simplifies some of our build logic. One thing we don’t support is FetchableDevEnvironment — we tried to make this work, but ulimately concluded that it forces frameworks to absorb too much complexity. We think the problems it aims to solve (most notably, providing access to Cloudflare Workers bindings during local development) can be addressed in other ways, which we’re actively exploring.

Remote functions

If you’ve been following SvelteKit’s development over the last year, you’ve likely encountered remote functions. This, alongside async Svelte, is our vision for how client-server communication should be handled.

We’re unreasonably excited about remote functions and can’t wait to use them everywhere. Frankly, they make everything else look a bit clunky, including SvelteKit’s load functions and actions.

For now, though, they remain behind an experimental flag as we iron out the last few kinks.

Send us your feedback

As ever, we rely on your thoughts and your bug reports: if you have the opportunity to upgrade your apps and test out the new stuff, we and the rest of the Svelte community will be in your debt. Thank you!

sentences.en: SvelteKit 3 requires Svelte 5, which means error handling can be made much more comprehensive and consistent.
sentences.zh: SvelteKit 3 需要 Svelte 5，这意味着错误处理可以更加全面和一致。

blocks.html_en: Another change is that all errors are piped through your handleError logic, including the ones you deliberately created with error(...) which were previously ignored on the assumption that you’d already done something with them. This gives you more flexibility with less hoop-jumping.

sentences.en: Another change is that all errors are piped through your handleError logic, including the ones you deliberately created with error(...)
sentences.zh: 另一个变化是所有错误都通过您的 handleError 逻辑进行管道传输，包括您故意使用 error(...) 创建的错误

sentences.en: which were previously ignored on the assumption that you’d already done something with them.

sentences.en: This gives you more flexibility with less hoop-jumping.
sentences.zh: 这可以让您更加灵活，减少跳圈次数。

blocks.html_en: Oh, and we apply sourcemaps to stack traces now. No biggie. (It’ll take a minute before every adapter can display properly sourcemapped stack traces in production, but this is the necessary first step.)

sentences.en: Oh, and we apply sourcemaps to stack traces now.
sentences.zh: 哦，我们现在将源映射应用于堆栈跟踪。

sentences.en: No biggie.
sentences.zh: 没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: (It’ll take a minute before every adapter can display properly sourcemapped stack traces in production, but this is the necessary first step.)
sentences.zh: （每个适配器都需要一分钟才能在生产中显示正确的源映射堆栈跟踪，但这是必要的第一步。）

blocks.html_en: Shallow routing now happens with goto

sentences.en: Shallow routing now happens with goto
sentences.zh: 浅层路由现在通过 goto 进行

blocks.html_en: Instead of using pushState and replaceState to use shallow routing, you now use goto with the shallow: true option. Shallow navigations now trigger beforeNavigate etc, and you can persist page state across a reload with persistState: true.

sentences.en: Instead of using pushState and replaceState to use shallow routing, you now use goto with the shallow: true option.
sentences.zh: 现在，您不再使用 PushState 和 ReplaceState 来使用浅层路由，而是将 goto 与shallow: true 选项结合使用。

sentences.en: Shallow navigations now trigger beforeNavigate etc, and you can persist page state across a reload with persistState: true.
sentences.zh: 浅层导航现在会触发 beforeNavigate 等，并且您可以使用 persistState: true 在重新加载时保留页面状态。

blocks.html_en: Vite 8: Rolldown, and the Environment API

sentences.en: Vite 8: Rolldown, and the Environment API
sentences.zh: Vite 8：Rolldown 和环境 API

blocks.html_en: SvelteKit 2 supported Vite 8, but SvelteKit 3 requires it. This means you get faster builds thanks to Rolldown.

sentences.en: SvelteKit 2 supported Vite 8, but SvelteKit 3 requires it.
sentences.zh: SvelteKit 2 支持 Vite 8，但 SvelteKit 3 需要它。

sentences.en: This means you get faster builds thanks to Rolldown.
sentences.zh: 这意味着您可以通过 Rolldown 获得更快的构建速度。

blocks.html_en: We’ve also adopted the Vite Environment API, which simplifies some of our build logic. One thing we don’t support is FetchableDevEnvironment — we tried to make this work, but ulimately concluded that it forces frameworks to absorb too much complexity. We think the problems it aims to solve (most notably, providing access to Cloudflare Workers bindings during local development) can be addressed in other ways, which we’re actively exploring.

sentences.en: We’ve also adopted the Vite Environment API, which simplifies some of our build logic.

sentences.en: One thing we don’t support is FetchableDevEnvironment — we tried to make this work, but ulimately concluded that it forces frameworks to absorb too much complexity.
sentences.zh: 我们不支持的一件事是 FetchableDevEnvironment——我们试图让这项工作发挥作用，但最终得出的结论是它迫使框架吸收太多的复杂性。

sentences.en: We think the problems it aims to solve (most notably, providing access to Cloudflare Workers bindings during local development) can be addressed in other ways, which we’re actively exploring.
sentences.zh: 我们认为它旨在解决的问题（最值得注意的是，在本地开发期间提供对 Cloudflare Workers 绑定的访问）可以通过其他方式解决，我们正在积极探索。

blocks.html_en: Remote functions

sentences.en: Remote functions
sentences.zh: 远程功能

blocks.html_en: If you’ve been following SvelteKit’s development over the last year, you’ve likely encountered remote functions. This, alongside async Svelte, is our vision for how client-server communication should be handled.

sentences.en: If you’ve been following SvelteKit’s development over the last year, you’ve likely encountered remote functions.
sentences.zh: 如果您去年一直关注 SvelteKit 的开发，您可能遇到过远程功能。

sentences.zh: 这与异步 Svelte 一起是我们对如何处理客户端-服务器通信的愿景。

blocks.html_en: We’re unreasonably excited about remote functions and can’t wait to use them everywhere. Frankly, they make everything else look a bit clunky, including SvelteKit’s load functions and actions.

sentences.en: We’re unreasonably excited about remote functions and can’t wait to use them everywhere.
sentences.zh: 我们对远程功能感到非常兴奋，迫不及待地想在任何地方使用它们。

blocks.html_en: For now, though, they remain behind an experimental flag as we iron out the last few kinks.

sentences.en: For now, though, they remain behind an experimental flag as we iron out the last few kinks.

blocks.html_en: Send us your feedback

blocks.html_en: As ever, we rely on your thoughts and your bug reports: if you have the opportunity to upgrade your apps and test out the new stuff, we and the rest of the Svelte community will be in your debt. Thank you!

content_html_zh:
SvelteKit 3 现在处于候选发布阶段。 如果一切顺利 - 意味着像您这样的人尝试并发现它按预期工作 - 我们将在不久的将来发布稳定版本，不再进行任何重大更改。

但自 SvelteKit 2 以来出现了一些重大变化。 我们正在利用这个版本来修剪代码库中的一些杂草，并为 SvelteKit 的持续发展奠定基础，更多内容见下文。

要迁移现有应用程序，您可以使用下一版本的 sv migrate：

npx sv@next migrate sveltekit-3 --tasks all --confirm

这将自动迁移尽可能多的代码。 对于其他所有事情，它都会生成一个 TODO 列表供您（或您选择的 clanr）完成。 如果您尝试运行尚未更新的代码，SvelteKit 将尽可能打印有用的诊断警告和错误。

要创建新应用程序，请运行 sv create：

npx sv@next create my-new-app

发生了什么变化？

有关更改的完整列表，请参阅 next.svelte.dev 上的迁移指南，在稳定版本发布之前，SvelteKit 3 文档将保存在此处。 大多数变化都很小，但有一些变化值得一提：

配置现在位于 vite.config.ts 中

以前，您可以通过 svelte.config.js 文件配置 SvelteKit。 事实证明，这是有限制的：Vite 插件可以立即访问您的配置，而不是必须经历异步解析过程（直到我们解析整个 Vite 配置之后才能开始，因为像 Vitest 这样的工具可能会使用不是项目根目录的当前工作目录运行），这很有用，毕竟我们为什么不将配置放在一个地方而不是两个地方呢？

$lib 别名现在是 #lib

在 SvelteKit 2 中，您可以将共享代码放入 src/lib 中，并通过 $lib 别名导入它。 这比从 ../../../../ 某个地方导入要好，这是在较大的代码库中不可避免地发生的情况。

但在现代项目中，别名是不必要的，因为我们有更好的东西：子路径导入。 Vite 和 TypeScript 等工具原生支持 Node 功能，这意味着我们可以删除之前在它们之间协调的代码。 有一个小问题：Node 和 TypeScript 要求您的子路径导入明确 - 您需要从 #lib/foo.ts 或 #lib/foo/index.ts 导入，而不是从 #lib/foo 导入。

TypeScript 配置变得更简单

在 SvelteKit 2 中，您的 tsconfig.json 需要扩展看起来有些邋遢的 ./.svelte-kit/tsconfig.json。 在 SvelteKit 3 中，您可以扩展 $app/tsconfig。 此生成的配置文件将写入 node_modules/$app 并包含特定于您的应用程序的配置。 虽然它比 SvelteKit 2 版本更简单（例如，我们不再需要向“paths”添加 $lib 别名），但它还包含更多推荐的编译器选项，这意味着您可以删除自己的编译器选项，除非您有深奥的要求。

您应该显式指定包含和排除数组，后者应包含您的服务工作人员。 说到这里：

服务人员整容了

在 SvelteKit 3 中使用 Service Worker 更好。 奇怪的 $service-worker 模块公开了执行离线缓存所需的工具（例如），您现在可以像应用程序的其他部分一样从 $app/env、$app/paths 和新的 $app/manifest 模块导入这些内容。 您还可以从 $app/service-worker 导入 self 以获得获取事件等的准确类型，前提是您与扩展 $app/tsconfig/service-worker 的 Service Worker 一起创建 tsconfig.json 。

将来，我们可能会为不同的缓存策略公开辅助函数，这样就可以更轻松地构建离线友好的 PWA 之类的东西，而不会遇到铁丝网。

环境变量更强大

SvelteKit 可以说是所有框架中最复杂、最灵活的环境变量处理。 SvelteKit 3 通过显式环境变量功能更进一步，该功能不再是实验性标志。 要点是，您在 src/env.ts 中定义您的应用程序依赖的环境变量，并指定它们是否应该公开可用（在这种情况下，您可以将它们导入到将在客户端中运行的代码中）以及它们是否应该在构建时解析（在这种情况下，它们可以用于诸如消除死代码之类的优化）或在应用程序启动时解析。 您还可以使用标准架构库来验证环境变量。

作为交换，您可以轻松获得类型安全、可靠、经过验证的环境变量，这些变量可以在您需要时自动导入。

错误处理更好

SvelteKit 2 受到对 Svelte 4 的支持的限制，Svelte 4 没有错误边界的概念。 这意味着我们只能在加载过程中发生错误时显示 +error.svelte 组件，而不能显示渲染过程中发生的错误。 SvelteKit 3 需要 Svelte 5，这意味着错误处理可以更加全面和一致。

另一个变化是所有错误都通过您的 handleError 逻辑进行管道传输，包括您故意使用 error(...) 创建的错误 之前假设您已经对它们做了一些事情，因此会忽略它们。 这可以让您更加灵活，减少跳圈次数。

哦，我们现在将源映射应用于堆栈跟踪。 没什么大不了的。 （每个适配器都需要一分钟才能在生产中显示正确的源映射堆栈跟踪，但这是必要的第一步。）

浅层路由现在通过 goto 进行

现在，您不再使用 PushState 和 ReplaceState 来使用浅层路由，而是将 goto 与shallow: true 选项结合使用。 浅层导航现在会触发 beforeNavigate 等，并且您可以使用 persistState: true 在重新加载时保留页面状态。

Vite 8：Rolldown 和环境 API

SvelteKit 2 支持 Vite 8，但 SvelteKit 3 需要它。 这意味着您可以通过 Rolldown 获得更快的构建速度。

我们还采用了 Vite 环境 API，它简化了我们的一些构建逻辑。 我们不支持的一件事是 FetchableDevEnvironment——我们试图让这项工作发挥作用，但最终得出的结论是它迫使框架吸收太多的复杂性。 我们认为它旨在解决的问题（最值得注意的是，在本地开发期间提供对 Cloudflare Workers 绑定的访问）可以通过其他方式解决，我们正在积极探索。

远程功能

如果您去年一直关注 SvelteKit 的开发，您可能遇到过远程功能。 这与异步 Svelte 一起是我们对如何处理客户端-服务器通信的愿景。

我们对远程功能感到非常兴奋，迫不及待地想在任何地方使用它们。 坦率地说，它们让其他一切看起来都有点笨拙，包括 SvelteKit 的加载函数和操作。

不过，就目前而言，当我们解决最后几个问题时，它们仍处于实验状态。

向我们发送您的反馈

一如既往，我们依赖您的想法和错误报告：如果您有机会升级您的应用程序并测试新内容，我们和 Svelte 社区的其他成员将感激您。 谢谢你！
